h1: The 8 Best Robot Pool Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Robot Pool Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot pool vacuums scored on pool size, waterline coverage and runtime, from AIPER cordless units to Dolphin Nautilus models.
summary: The AIPER Scuba V3 is the one to buy for most pools: AI vision navigation, cordless, and it cleans floor, walls and waterline. For the most coverage, the AIPER Scuba S1 runs up to 270 minutes. If you have a big in-ground pool, the Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus is rated to 40 feet. For a small above-ground pool, the Y20 is sized sensibly.
intro: The first mistake pool owners make with a robot cleaner is buying for brand instead of for pool shape. A cleaner built for a flat 15 foot above-ground pool will skip the steps and ledges in a 35 foot in-ground one, and a cleaner built for walls will struggle on a pool that needs floor coverage most.

So the ranking starts with pool size and bottom type, then adds runtime, waterline ability and whether the cleaner is cordless or corded. We reviewed eight models from AIPER, Dolphin and newer makers, scored them on the Primea framework, and noted which pool each really suits.

products.name: AIPER Scuba V3 AI Vision Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: AI vision mapping, no cord, and floor-to-waterline cleaning. The most capable cordless unit here.
products.description:
The Scuba V3 uses AI vision to map the pool and plan its path, rather than bouncing around at random like older cordless cleaners. It handles the floor, the walls and the waterline in one cycle, and the basket opens from the top for quick emptying.

It wins because it solves the two chores people hate most: untangling a cord and scrubbing the waterline. It costs more than the budget cordless units below and gives you a smarter path in return. Against the S1, you give up some runtime in exchange for the vision system.

Best for a typical in-ground pool where you want a set-and-forget cleaner with complete coverage.
cons: Runtime shorter than the Scuba S1
products.idealFor: Typical in-ground pools needing full coverage.
products.skipIf: You have a small above-ground pool and want the cheapest option.

products.name: AIPER Scuba S1 Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: 270 minutes of runtime, 11 sensors and shallow-area cleaning. Built for irregular pools.
products.description:
The Scuba S1 lists a 270 minute runtime, among the longest in the guide, plus 11 sensors, app control and weekly custom scheduling. It cleans the floor, walls, waterline and shallow areas such as steps and tanning ledges that flat-bottom cleaners skip.

It sits behind the V3 because that model uses AI vision to plan its route, while the S1 leans on sensors and long battery life. For a large or oddly shaped pool, the extra runtime is the better asset, so this is the one to buy if coverage and time on the clock matter more than the smartest routing.

Good for larger pools and any pool with ledges, steps or shallow shelves.
products.idealFor: Large or irregular pools with ledges and steps.
products.skipIf: Your pool is small and flat.

products.name: Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus Robotic Pool Vacuum
products.verdict: Corded, wall-climbing and rated for in-ground pools up to 40 feet. The big-pool workhorse.
products.description:
The Nautilus CC Plus steps up from the standard CC with a rating for in-ground pools up to 40 feet and smart navigation designed to cut overlap and missed spots. It keeps the wall-climbing scrubber brush that Dolphin is known for.

Against the cordless AIPERs, you accept a cord in exchange for no battery to worry about, so there is no recharge between sessions. That matters on a large pool, where a battery cleaner may stop before it is finished. Compared with the standard CC, you pay more for the extra seven feet of rated length.

Best for large in-ground pools where you want a corded machine that simply keeps running.
products.idealFor: Large in-ground pools up to 40 feet.
products.skipIf: You dislike cords or have an above-ground pool.

products.name: Dolphin Nautilus CC Automatic Robotic Pool Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A proven corded cleaner with a scrubber brush for walls. Rated for pools up to 33 feet.
products.description:
Dolphin has made pool cleaners for years, and the Nautilus CC pairs a dedicated scrubber brush with top-load filter access. It suits above-ground and in-ground pools up to 33 feet long, which covers most residential pools.

It ranks just under the CC Plus because the Plus is rated for 40 feet and adds smarter navigation. If your pool is 33 feet or shorter, that extra capability is unnecessary and the standard CC is the sensible buy.

Choose it for average-sized pools where algae on the walls is the main problem.
pros: Scrubber brush for walls and algae
cons: Lower length rating than the Plus
products.idealFor: Average pools up to 33 feet with algae-prone walls.
products.skipIf: Your pool is longer than 33 feet.

products.name: Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner, 180-Min Runtime, 3L Basket
products.verdict: 180 minutes, a 3L basket and coverage up to 2200 sq ft. The cordless value choice.
products.description:
This cordless cleaner lists a 180 minute runtime, a 3 litre basket and auto-parking, and is rated for pools up to 2200 square feet, above-ground or in-ground. The large basket handles leaves better than fine-sediment-only baskets.

It is the budget pick because it covers a lot of ground for the money. What it lacks is the smart routing and waterline focus of the AIPER models above, so expect a plainer cleaning pattern. It still finishes most residential pools in one cycle.

A good fit for owners who want cordless convenience and a big basket on a smaller budget.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting cordless with a big basket.
products.skipIf: Waterline scum is your main concern.

products.name: EZIOOV U8 Cordless Robotic Pool Cleaner
products.verdict: Built around wall and waterline cleaning with auto-climb and auto-docking.
products.description:
The U8 is built around wall and waterline work, climbing automatically, docking itself and running 150 minutes for in-ground pools up to 2600 square feet. A scummy waterline is what makes a pool look neglected.

It ranks sixth because it is a newer name without the track record of AIPER or Dolphin, and the 150 minute runtime is shorter than the S1 and budget 180 minute unit. It makes sense when the walls and tile line are your main chore.

Best for in-ground pools where you are tired of hand-scrubbing the waterline.
products.skipIf: Floor debris is your main problem.

products.name: Y20 Robotic Pool Cleaner for Above Ground and Flat Pools
products.verdict: Dual motors and auto-parking for small flat pools up to 1100 sq ft.
products.description:
The Y20 targets small above-ground pools and flat in-ground pools of up to 1100 square feet, and has dual motors, a 120 minute runtime and auto-parking. Dual motors give steadier suction on a flat floor than single-motor budget units.

It ranks lower because it is limited by size and bottom type, so it does not cover larger or sloped pools. Within that range it is a sensible purchase, because you do not pay for coverage a small pool never uses.

A fit for owners of standard above-ground pools.
pros: Dual motors on a flat floor
products.skipIf: Your pool is large or has a sloped bottom.

products.name: Coasteering Planet Edge Pool Vacuum for Above Ground Pool
products.verdict: A compact dual-motor unit for flat above-ground pools up to 850 sq ft.
products.description:
The Planet Edge is built for small flat-bottom above-ground pools, with dual motors, a 120 minute runtime and an adjustable cleaning path so it does not wander randomly. Its compact build makes it easy to lift out and store.

It ranks last because its 850 square foot limit is the smallest in the guide, so it only suits pools of that size. If yours fits, the light weight is a real daily convenience.

Good for small flat pools where carrying the cleaner in and out is a regular task.

whatMatters.detail: Cleaners are rated by pool length or square footage. Measure your pool in feet and compare it with the stated limit, which might be 33 feet, 40 feet or 2200 sq ft. A cleaner rated below your size will run out of battery or miss areas.

Cordless units need no cable and are easy to move but run on battery, so check the runtime in minutes against your pool size. Corded units keep running but the cord can tangle on steps and ladders. Read the listing for the minutes figure.
Many budget cordless units are for flat-bottom pools only. Sloped or deep-end pools need a cleaner that climbs and keeps traction. Look for the words flat pools in the title or specs.
The waterline is where oils and scum collect. Cleaners that list waterline cleaning or auto-climb do the tile line, while floor-only models leave it. Check the spec bullets.
A 3 litre basket takes leaves better than a small fine-debris filter. A top-load design lets you empty it without lifting the whole unit out. Look for basket litres and access type.

faq.q: How long should a robot pool cleaner run?
faq.a: Match runtime to pool size. A 120 minute unit like the Y20 suits a small flat pool, while the AIPER Scuba S1 at 270 minutes is better for large or irregular pools.

faq.q: Do robot pool cleaners climb walls?
faq.a: Some do. The Dolphin Nautilus CC models and the EZIOOV U8 list wall climbing or auto-climb. Flat-pool models like the Y20 and Planet Edge are for the floor only.

faq.q: Is the AIPER Scuba V3 worth more than a budget cordless model?
faq.a: If you want AI vision routing and waterline coverage, yes. For simple floor cleaning on a smaller pool, the budget 180-minute unit does the basics for less.

faq.q: Can a cordless cleaner run on a large pool?
faq.a: Only if its battery lasts long enough. Check the runtime against pool size. For pools around 40 feet, a corded Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus avoids battery limits.

faq.q: How often should I empty the basket?
faq.a: After every cycle if you have trees nearby, otherwise weekly. A full basket reduces suction. Top-load designs like the AIPER Scuba V3 make this quick.

faq.q: Do I need to take the cleaner out of the pool?
faq.a: Cordless cleaners with auto-parking, such as the 180-minute unit and Y20, park at the wall for easy retrieval. Always remove it before shocking the pool or letting it sit for days.

finalTake: For most pools the AIPER Scuba V3 is the right buy: AI vision, cordless, and floor to waterline coverage. If your pool is large or has ledges, the AIPER Scuba S1 gives 270 minutes of runtime. Got a big in-ground pool and do not mind a cord? The Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus is rated to 40 feet. And for small above-ground pools, the Y20 does the job without paying for coverage you do not need.
